QF.id: Cat III AIF Overview and Growth_22

question.text: Hedge Funds are characteristic of HIGHER risk taking compared to other AIFs because:

answer.text: They use significant leverage at fund level

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 18-19 of the source explain that hedge funds differ from other AIFs by using complex strategies, long/short positions and significant fund-level leverage. The page 19 footnote makes the risk argument explicit — fund-level borrowings must be repaid regardless of gains or losses, which amplifies overall investment risk. The Trap: Investing in gold, having shorter duration, or having a lower AUM are not the primary risk drivers; the structural use of leverage is. Note: Page 46 also links Category III AIF risk specifically to leverage and derivative exposures.
